verses.1: The people who lived in Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the raiding band that came from the Arabs at evening had killed all the older ones. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram became king over Judah.
verses.2: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Atalyah, daughter of Omri.
verses.3: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab, for his mother was the one who advised him to do evil.
verses.4: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, just as the house of Ahab did, for his own mother had been his counselors after his father’s death, to destroy him.
verses.5: By their advice he went and joined Jehoram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. But the Arameans shot Jehoram.
verses.6: He returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds he had received in the battle with Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Israel, because he was sick.
verses.7: But this was from the LORD, the ruin of Ahaziah going to see Jehoram. And when he went out with him, he went with Jehoram to Jehu son of Nimshi, the one anointed by the LORD to cut off the house of Ahab.
verses.8: And when Jehu judged the house of Ahab, he found the commanders of Judah and the brothers of Ahaziah serving Ahaziah. He struck them down.
verses.9: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu, and he put him to death. They buried him, because they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” There was no one in the house of Ahaziah who had the strength to hold the kingdom.
verses.10: Atalyah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead. She rose and destroyed all the royal descendants of the house of Judah.
verses.11: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being killed. She put him and his nurse in the bedroom chamber and hid him. Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah, concealed him from Atalyah, and she did not kill him.
verses.12: He remained with her in the house of God for six years, while Atalyah reigned over the land.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "to be healed in Israel" reflects the context that Jehoram was in Israel, not that Ahaziah was healed in Israel specifically.
- v. 7: "this was from the LORD" is a translation of "מֵֽאֱלֹהִים הָיְתָה תְּבוּסַת" as a divine arrangement or judgment.
- v. 9: “he was hiding in Samaria” is a natural interpretation of the Hebrew, which says he was hiding and was captured there.
raw:
[1] The people who lived in Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the raiding band that came from the Arabs at evening had killed all the older ones. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram became king over Judah.

[2] Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Atalyah, daughter of Omri.

[3] He walked in the way of the house of Ahab, for his mother was the one who advised him to do evil.

[4] He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, just as the house of Ahab did, for his own mother had been his counselors after his father’s death, to destroy him.

[5] By their advice he went and joined Jehoram the son of Ahab, king of Israel, to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. But the Arameans shot Jehoram.

[6] He returned to be healed in Israel from the wounds he had received in the battle with Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Israel, because he was sick.

[7] But this was from the LORD, the ruin of Ahaziah going to see Jehoram. And when he went out with him, he went with Jehoram to Jehu son of Nimshi, the one anointed by the LORD to cut off the house of Ahab.

[8] And when Jehu judged the house of Ahab, he found the commanders of Judah and the brothers of Ahaziah serving Ahaziah. He struck them down.

[9] He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu, and he put him to death. They buried him, because they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” There was no one in the house of Ahaziah who had the strength to hold the kingdom.

[10] Atalyah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead. She rose and destroyed all the royal descendants of the house of Judah.

[11] But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being killed. She put him and his nurse in the bedroom chamber and hid him. Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah, concealed him from Atalyah, and she did not kill him.

[12] He remained with her in the house of God for six years, while Atalyah reigned over the land.

---
Notes
- v. 6: "to be healed in Israel" reflects the context that Jehoram was in Israel, not that Ahaziah was healed in Israel specifically.
- v. 7: "this was from the LORD" is a translation of "מֵֽאֱלֹהִים הָיְתָה תְּבוּסַת" as a divine arrangement or judgment.
- v. 9: “he was hiding in Samaria” is a natural interpretation of the Hebrew, which says he was hiding and was captured there.
